candidates.coupling_risks: Primary operand reads alter reset-selector provenance; secondary reads do not. Loops can skip unavailable target bytes. Instructions may overlap headers/presets/other stream roles, so compilation must not partition bytes into disjoint presumed streams or reject unused partial entries.
candidates.bounded_reason: Complete primary and secondary sequence format/executors and immutable asset owner, including note decoding and source read boundaries. Oscillators, synthesizer, queue and channel arithmetic remain source-contracted and shared across platforms.
candidates.strongest_conversion_considered: Immutable typed programs for both interpreters selected, including every imported byte entry to preserve overlapping and synthetic starts. Local enum decode/reencode or a cache that can become stale beside publicly mutable fragments is insufficient.
candidates.remaining_boundary_encodings: Original resource locations remain necessary for public source cursor observations, branch identity and actual read-derived reset seeds. Private raw asset data remains only for genuine preset/period/header consumers. Packed channel fields remain observable through canonical reset-alias projections; instruction encodings disappear from playback.
removed_machinery: raw sequence opcode dispatch in both playback interpreters
candidates.contract_adaptations: Synthetic catalog construction now uses explicit fragment import/add methods; file-authored overlays use explicit prepend/recompile.
